fields.features_heading: What a Pay per Call Page Needs
fields.features_subheading: The buyer pays for the call, not the visit. Describe the offer and its terms, and Emergent builds a page made for the phone.
fields.feature_1:
A number that dials on a phone

Emergent builds your tracking number into a tel: link in the header and again under the offer. On a cell phone, one tap on that link dials the number, with no digits to retype.
fields.feature_2:
One tracking number per page

Give each page the number the buyer or network assigned to that campaign. The page shows that number in every call button, and each call ties back to the page that drew it.
fields.feature_3:
Every tap saved as a row

The app saves each tap on a call button to a database you own, with the page, the button, the time, and the campaign tag from the ad link. Sort the rows by hour or by campaign.
fields.feature_4:
Call lengths from your tracker

Connect the call tracking tool you use over its API, and the app pulls each call's length next to the tap that started it. Calls past the buyer's minimum get marked billable.
fields.feature_5:
Hours that match the buyer's

Set the hours the buyer answers calls. Outside them, the page shows a short callback form in place of the call button, and the app emails each request to your dispatcher.
fields.feature_6:
The page as code you keep

Export the page and its tap log to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Or host it on Emergent under a custom domain, which uses credits, and change the copy by prompt.

fields.usecase_heading: Pay per Call Landing Page Examples
fields.tab_content_1:
Columbus callers who stayed on past 90 seconds

Quillfen Media sends Columbus furnace repair callers to a buyer that pays only for calls over 90 seconds. The page shows the buyer's tracking number as a call button, and the app marks each call past 90 seconds using lengths from the call tracking tool. Of 214 calls in October, 131 ran long enough to bill.
fields.tab_content_2:
Wichita's number drew 58 taps in a single week

Tovenhall Leads keeps a separate pest control page for Tulsa, Wichita, and Omaha, each with the tracking number its buyer assigned. One prompt built all three pages on the same layout. Last week the pages drew 132 call taps between them: 58 in Wichita, 41 in Tulsa, and 33 in Omaha.
fields.tab_content_3:
After 7 p.m., a callback form takes the button's place

Brisworth Plumbing Network answers calls between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. After hours, the page hides the call button and shows a callback form asking for a name, a phone number, and the problem. The app emails the overnight list to the dispatcher, Marit Vesterholt, at 7 a.m. Last week, 22 requests came in overnight.
fields.tab_content_4:
With hail in the headline, call taps rose to 114

Ridgewane Roofing ran two headlines on its Denver page, each shown to 1,200 visitors. The plain one, "Roof repair in Denver", drew 72 call taps. "Hail damage? Call a Denver roofer" drew 114. The app counts taps per headline in one table, and the hail version now runs alone.

fields.howto_title: How to Create Pay per Call Landing Pages
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to pay per call landing pages that turn ad visitors into calls a buyer pays for, then build them with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Get the buyer's call terms in writing
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put the number within thumb reach
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Match the page to the ad
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Give each campaign its own number
fields.howto_step_1_des: Ask the buyer or network for the minimum call length, the hours they answer, and the areas they accept. Write those terms down with the date you got them. Every later choice on the page follows from them, including what visitors see after hours.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Place a call button in the header, then a second one right under the offer. Label the button with an action, such as Call for a repair today. Keep the digits visible as well, for visitors on a laptop who dial from a desk phone.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Repeat the ad's promise in the headline, word for word where you can, and name the city or service the ad named. A visitor who searched for hail damage repair should read hail damage before anything else on the page.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Use a separate tracking number for each page or traffic source you want to count apart. Ask the buyer which number belongs to which campaign before launch, and keep that list next to the call log for the first month.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Plan for the hours nobody answers
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide what a visitor sees when the buyer's line is closed. A callback form with three fields suits urgent repairs. A plain line with the opening hours suits the rest. Either one beats a call that rings out with no one there to pick up.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Tell Emergent the offer, the number to show, the open hours, and which calls count. Emergent builds the page and the table that saves each call tap, and you change any part later by sending another message.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Call the page from your own phone
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before ads go live, tap the button on a phone and stay on the line past the buyer's minimum. Check that the tap shows in the log with the right page and campaign, then repeat the test outside the buyer's hours.

faq_plan.q: What are pay per call landing pages?
faq_plan.a: Pay per call landing pages are pages built to get a visitor to phone a business instead of filling in a form. The call button carries a tracking number, and the advertiser pays the publisher for each quality call the page produces.

faq_plan.q: How do I create pay per call landing pages?
faq_plan.a: List the offer, the tracking number, the buyer's schedule, and the minimum call length. Then describe the page to Emergent's AI landing page builder in one message. Emergent builds the page with its call buttons and a table of every tap, and edits it when you ask.

faq_plan.q: How long does a call need to last to count on pay per call landing pages?
faq_plan.a: There is no single length: the advertiser decides. Invoca says advertisers set the criteria that define if a call is commissionable, typically based on the length of the phone call. The date and time of a call can count as well, and so can its region.

faq_plan.q: What should pay per call landing pages leave out?
faq_plan.a: Leave out anything that pulls a visitor away from the call, such as a site menu or links to other offers. Keep one service area and one number per page. Emergent builds a single-purpose page from a plain-English prompt, and removes a section when you ask.

faq_plan.q: Do pay per call landing pages need a form?
faq_plan.a: Not as the main action, since the call button does that job. A short callback form earns its place after the buyer stops answering for the day, or for visitors who cannot talk right then. Ask only for what the buyer needs to call back.

faq_plan.q: How are calls from pay per call landing pages tracked to their source?
faq_plan.a: Through the tracking number. In Invoca's setup, each publisher or campaign is assigned a specific phone number, and a call to that number is tied to the original source. For finer detail, a small snippet of code on a landing page fills in unique tracking numbers automatically.

faq_plan.q: Do repeat callers count on pay per call landing pages?
faq_plan.a: Usually not. Invoca notes that unanswered calls or repeat calls do not typically qualify for commission. Ask the buyer how long a caller counts as repeat, such as 30 days, and mark repeat numbers in your own log so your counts match theirs.

faq_plan.q: How do I make the number on pay per call landing pages tap to call?
faq_plan.a: Wrap the number in a tel: link. MDN notes that tel: link behavior varies with device capabilities, and that cellular devices autodial the number. On a laptop, keep the digits large and readable for anyone who dials by hand.

faq_plan.q: Should pay per call landing pages be built one per city?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the buyer accepts calls by area or you want to count cities apart. A page per city lets the headline name the city and carry its own number. Emergent builds the set from one prompt, and each page's taps land in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How are pay per call landing pages different from pay per click pages?
faq_plan.a: A pay per click page is paid for per ad click, and its goal can be a form fill or a sale. A pay per call page has one goal, a phone call. In Invoca's words, an advertiser pays publishers for quality calls generated on the advertiser's behalf.
